mainTopic: The sources for קידושין by שטר, why money cannot divorce, why all three methods of קידושין are needed, and רב הונא's claim that חופה acquires
overview: The ברייתא asks how we know a woman can be betrothed with a שטר. A קל וחומר from כסף fails, so it learns this from the היקש of 'וְיָצְאָה... וְהָיְתָה', which links betrothal to divorce. The גמרא asks why the link does not also let money divorce. אביי says the thing that joins a couple should not separate them, and explains why documents differ from coins. רבא instead learns from 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' that only writing divorces. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת'. The רבנן use כריתות to teach that a גט must fully cut the bond, so a condition that lasts forever ruins it. The גמרא then shows that none of the three ways of making קידושין (כסף, שטר, ביאה) can be learned from the other two. Finally רב הונא argues by קל וחומר that חופה also makes קידושין. After עולא knocks down the תרומה version, the גמרא begins rewording the proof, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a document can effect betrothal?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that קידושין can also be done with a שטר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that a woman can be betrothed even with a document?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא already showed that money works for קידושין, and now it asks for the source for the second method, a document. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אף' (even) tells us money was already covered. Now the ברייתא needs a separate source for שטר, because a document has no money value of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asking for a source)
A document; here, a betrothal document
Even / also

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it can also be done with a document?
phrases.notes: 'It' means betrothing a woman. The money way was already proven earlier in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא after it has already proven that money effects קידושין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a שטר can effect קידושין.

steps.title: A logical argument from money to document
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tries a קל וחומר: money cannot divorce yet still betroths, so a document, which does divorce, should surely betroth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical: if money, which cannot release a woman from marriage, can still bring her into marriage, then surely a document, which can release her, should also be able to bring her in.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with logic instead of a פסוק. It uses a קל וחומר to argue that a document is 'stronger' than money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument says a document has proven power in marriage law, since a גט ends a marriage, while money has no power to end one. If the weaker item (money) can start a marriage, the stronger item (document) should be able to as well.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a logical argument (it can be figured out by reasoning)
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
Takes out, meaning ends a marriage (divorce)
Brings in, meaning starts a marriage (betrothal)

phrases.english: And it is a logical argument:
If money, which does not take out, still brings in,
then a document, which does take out, is it not logical that it brings in?
phrases.notes: A document 'takes out' because a גט is a document, and a גט ends a marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with a logical argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from money: a document, which can end a marriage, should certainly be able to start one.

steps.title: Money has a special power that a document lacks
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר is rejected: money can redeem הקדש and מעשר שני, which a document cannot, so money may simply be stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about money? Money is special, since it can redeem consecrated property and second tithe. Can you say the same about a document, which cannot redeem them? We know only money redeems, because it is written: 'And he shall give the money and it will be his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down its own logical argument. It shows that money has a strength a document does not have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'weaker' case really is weaker in every relevant way. Money turns out to be stronger in one area, since it can redeem holy property, so maybe that is why it can betroth. The argument from money to document therefore falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? (pointing out a unique feature to break a comparison)
Redeem (release from holiness by paying)
Property that has been made holy for the בית המקדש
Second tithe, which can be redeemed with money

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying a document is weaker overall. It only shows that money has its own special strength, so we cannot prove from money that a document works.

phrases.english: What about money? It is special, since one can redeem with it
consecrated property and second tithe.
Will you say the same about a document, with which one cannot redeem
consecrated property and second tithe,
as it is written: 'And he shall give the money and it will be his'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:19

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְכֶסֶף, שֶׁכֵּן פּוֹדִין בּוֹ הֶקְדֵּשׁ וּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire קל וחומר from money to document.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Money has a unique power, redeeming הקדש and מעשר שני, that a document lacks, so money is not the 'weaker' case.

steps.title: A פסוק links betrothal to divorce
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וְיָצְאָה... וְהָיְתָה' links becoming married to leaving a marriage. Since leaving is done with a document, so is becoming.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And she leaves... and she becomes [another man's wife].' It compares becoming to leaving: just as leaving is done with a document, so too becoming can be done with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic failed, the ברייתא brings a source from a פסוק. It uses a היקש, a comparison the פסוק itself makes by putting two words side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'leaving' (divorce) right next to 'becoming' (a new marriage), which tells us to treat them alike. Divorce works through a document (a גט), so betrothal can also work through a document.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (makes a היקש between two things)
'Becoming', meaning entering a marriage
'Leaving', meaning divorce

steps.whatToRemember: קידושין with a שטר is learned from the היקש of הויה to יציאה in the פסוק 'וְיָצְאָה... וְהָיְתָה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real source that a document can effect קידושין, one of the three methods listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And she leaves' 'and she becomes'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2

phrases.english: It compares becoming to leaving:
Just as leaving is through a document,
so too becoming is also through a document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected logical argument with a פסוק-based היקש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש from 'וְיָצְאָה... וְהָיְתָה': betrothal is like divorce, so it can be done with a document.

steps.title: Why not compare the other way too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if betrothal and divorce are linked, divorce should be possible with money, just as betrothal is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us also compare leaving to becoming: just as becoming can be done with money, so too leaving should be possible with money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the היקש by running it in reverse. If the comparison works in one direction, why shouldn't it work in both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש usually makes the two items alike in both directions. If so, money, which works for betrothal, should also work for divorce. That conclusion is wrong, because divorce needs a גט, so the גמרא needs to explain why the comparison only goes one way.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us compare (in the other direction)
Also

phrases.english: And let us also compare leaving to becoming:
Just as becoming is through money,
so too leaving should be through money!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the היקש of step 4 by reversing its direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The one-directional use of the היקש between הויה and יציאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A היקש should apply both ways, which would allow divorce with money, and we know that is not the halacha.

steps.title: אביי: what joins a couple should not separate them
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that money cannot divorce, since it would look wrong for the thing that brought a couple together to also break them apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: People would say, 'Money brings in and money takes out.' Should a defense lawyer become a prosecutor?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge with a reason based on what is fitting. Money was the 'friend' that joined the couple, so it should not be the tool that splits them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money played the role of the 'defense lawyer' (סניגור) for the marriage by creating it. Using money to end the marriage would turn that same helper into the 'prosecutor' (קטיגור). So the reverse היקש is blocked for money.

keyTerms.meaning: People will say
A defense lawyer, one who speaks in someone's favor
A prosecutor, one who speaks against someone

phrases.english: אביי said:
People will say: Money brings in, money takes out,
should a defense lawyer become a prosecutor?
phrases.notes: He means it is not fitting for the thing that created the marriage to be used to destroy it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: יֹאמְרוּ: כֶּסֶף מַכְנִיס, כֶּסֶף מוֹצִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reason of fittingness: the reverse היקש is blocked because the same item should not both create and end a marriage.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The היקש should work both ways, so money could divorce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money cannot divorce, because a 'סניגור' should not become a 'קטיגור'.

steps.title: The same logic should block a document from betrothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: a document ends a marriage, so by his logic it should not also start one, like a prosecutor turning into a defense lawyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, people will also say about a document: 'A document takes out and a document brings in.' Should a prosecutor become a defense lawyer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns אביי's own reasoning against the step 4 source. If one item should not play both roles, then a document, which divorces, should not be able to betroth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's principle seems to cut both ways. A document is the 'prosecutor' because it ends marriages, so letting it create marriages would turn a prosecutor into a defense lawyer. That would undo the היקש that allowed קידושין with a שטר, so the גמרא needs an answer, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your reasoning is correct)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the document method has been rejected. The next step answers this challenge.

phrases.english: If so, about a document too
people will say: A document takes out, a document brings in,
should a prosecutor become a defense lawyer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses אביי's answer from step 6 to challenge the conclusion of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's principle as applied together with the היקש allowing קידושין with a שטר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one item may not both create and end a marriage, a document, which ends marriages, should not be able to create them either.

steps.title: Two documents have different wording
steps.stepSummary: A קידושין document and a גט say different things, so they are not really 'the same thing' doing opposite jobs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words of this document are separate, and the words of that document are separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. A document can both start and end a marriage because the betrothal document and the divorce document have completely different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 argued that a document ends a marriage, so by אביי's logic it should not start one. The answer is that it is not the same document. Each שטר is written with its own content, so nobody sees it as one object switching sides.

keyTerms.meaning: words, contents
a document
separate, on its own

phrases.english: The words of this document are separate
phrases.notes: This one is the betrothal document.

phrases.english: and the words of this document are separate.
phrases.notes: This one is the גט, the divorce document.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילֵּי דְּהַאי שְׁטָרָא לְחוֹד וּמִילֵּי דְּהַאי שְׁטָרָא לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 against אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the two documents differ in content.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A document ends a marriage, so it would look wrong for a document to also create one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The documents are different texts, so there is no look of one thing doing both jobs.

steps.title: But two coins are also separate coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the betrothal coin and a divorce coin would also be two different coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, this money is separate and that money is separate!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 8. If separate documents are fine, separate coins should be fine too, so money should be able to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man would not give back the same coin he used for קידושין. A new coin would be used for the divorce, so the 'same thing both joins and separates' problem seems to disappear for money as well.

keyTerms.meaning: here too, the same applies here
money, a coin

phrases.english: Here too, this money is separate
phrases.notes: The coin used for the קידושין.

phrases.english: and that money is separate!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, הַאי כַּסְפָּא לְחוֹד וְהַאי כַּסְפָּא לְחוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of step 8 to attack אביי's reason in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reason that money cannot divorce (step 6), as defended in step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being a separate object solves the problem for documents, it should solve it for coins too.

steps.title: A coin is a coin
steps.stepSummary: Coins all look the same, so a divorce coin would look exactly like the betrothal coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, a coin is one and the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that coins are not really different from each other the way documents are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document is defined by its words, so two documents are clearly two different things. A coin has no special content, so any coin looks like the coin that made the marriage. That is why אביי's concern still applies to money but not to a שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: a coin
in any case, still
it is one, the same

steps.whatToRemember: A שטר can both make and end a marriage because each document has its own wording. Money cannot divorce because all coins look the same, so it would look like the same thing joining and separating.

phrases.english: Still, the coin is one and the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and closes אביי's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: coins are identical, documents are not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two different coins are as separate as two different documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: A coin carries no unique content, so all coins count as 'one'.

steps.title: רבא: 'And he writes her' means divorce only by writing
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different source: the פסוק says the husband writes, so divorce works only with writing, not money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The verse says 'And he writes her.' She is divorced by writing, and she is not divorced by money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new reason, from a פסוק, why money cannot divorce, instead of אביי's logic about appearances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' tell us a divorce is done through writing. רבא reads this as excluding any other method, so money cannot end a marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: and he writes her (a גט)
writing
she is divorced

phrases.english: רבא said:
The verse says: 'And he writes her'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:3

phrases.english: through writing she is divorced,
and she is not divorced through money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of step 5, different from אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divorce works only through writing, so money cannot divorce.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק excludes betrothal by writing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way to read the פסוק: writing is for divorce, not for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: she is divorced through writing, and she is not betrothed through writing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading of 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' with a different way to understand what it excludes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exclusion from a פסוק needs a target. Instead of 'only writing divorces,' it could mean 'writing is only for divorce,' which would remove שטר from קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: but say instead
she becomes betrothed

phrases.english: But say instead: through writing she is divorced,
and she is not betrothed through writing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same exclusion could just as easily be read as blocking a document from creating קידושין.

steps.title: The link of 'leaving' and 'becoming' already teaches betrothal by document
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וְיָצְאָה... וְהָיְתָה' links betrothal to divorce, so a document must work for קידושין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'And she leaves... and becomes,' which links them, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' cannot exclude betrothal by document, because another פסוק already teaches that a document does make קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 showed that becoming married is compared to leaving a marriage. Since leaving is done with a document, so is becoming married. So 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' must be excluding something else: money from divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: and she leaves (the marriage) and becomes (another's wife)
it compares, links (a הקש)

phrases.english: But it is written: 'And she leaves' 'and becomes'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2

phrases.english: it compares, and so on.
phrases.notes: 'And so on' points back to step 4: becoming married is compared to leaving, so a document works for both.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by pointing back to the הקש of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another פסוק blocks the alternative reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' might exclude betrothal by document.
steps.terutzMaskana: The הקש already proves a document works for קידושין, so 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' excludes money from divorce.

steps.title: Why read it this way and not the reverse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we choose this reading, when the opposite reading also seems possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we use the הקש for documents and 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' against money, instead of the other way around. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could flip it: use the הקש to say money works for both betrothal and divorce, and use 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' to say writing is only for divorce. The גמרא wants a reason to prefer one reading.

keyTerms.meaning: and what did you see? (why choose this)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sources are still in play. The question is only which job each one does: which one excludes, and which one links.

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why did you pick this reading and not the reverse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice of readings made in steps 11 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way steps 11 and 13 split the jobs of the two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reverse reading seems just as possible, so the choice needs a reason.

steps.title: A פסוק about divorce excludes a way of divorcing
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense that a פסוק talking about divorce limits divorce, not betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense: when it speaks about divorce, it excludes a kind of divorce. Would it speak about divorce and exclude a kind of betrothal?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its choice: 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' is about divorce, so whatever it excludes must also be about divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An exclusion naturally applies to the topic the פסוק is discussing. Since 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' is about divorce, it excludes money from divorce. It would be strange for it to suddenly limit קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, it is logical
it is dealing with, talking about
excludes
divorce

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's source: 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' means only writing divorces, so money cannot. It limits divorce, not betrothal, because the פסוק is talking about divorce.

phrases.english: It makes sense: when it speaks about divorce, it excludes a kind of divorce;
would it speak about divorce and exclude a kind of betrothal?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 and closes רבא's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical reasoning: an exclusion stays within the topic of its פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' could just as well limit betrothal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the פסוק is about divorce, it excludes money from divorce.

steps.title: What is רבי יוסי הגלילי's source?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי uses 'וְכָתַב לָהּ' to teach something else, so where does he learn that money cannot divorce?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, who uses this verse for a different teaching, where does he learn that she cannot be divorced with money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for one תנא who cannot use רבא's פסוק. It is setting up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof depends on 'וְכָתַב לָהּ'. Since רבי יוסי הגלילי already needs those words for another teaching, he must learn the rule against divorce by money from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: who takes it out (uses it) for
a different teaching from the פסוק
where does he learn it from?

phrases.english: And according to רבי יוסי הגלילי,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהַאי קְרָא לִדְרָשָׁא אַחֲרִינָא,
phrases.english: who uses this verse for a different teaching,
phrases.notes: 'This verse' means 'וְכָתַב לָהּ', the words רבא used.

phrases.english: from where does he learn that she is not divorced through money?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לְהַאי קְרָא לִדְרָשָׁא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the rule of step 11 works for someone who cannot use רבא's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source that money cannot divorce.

steps.title: 'A scroll of severance': only a scroll cuts the marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת' that only a document ends the marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'a scroll of severance': a scroll cuts her off, and nothing else cuts her off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's source: the words 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת' teach that only a written document ends a marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins 'scroll' with 'cutting off,' meaning the scroll is what does the cutting. Anything else, including money, cannot end the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: a scroll of severance, a גט
cuts her off, separates her
anything else

steps.whatToRemember: Three ways to explain why money cannot divorce: אביי's logic (it would look wrong), רבא's פסוק 'וְכָתַב לָהּ', and רבי יוסי הגלילי's פסוק 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת'.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'A scroll of severance':
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

phrases.english: a scroll cuts her off,
and nothing else cuts her off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת': only a document severs the marriage, so money cannot.

steps.title: What do the רבנן do with the word כריתות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן use the word כריתות, since they did not use it the way רבי יוסי הגלילי did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word כריתות?
steps.whatsHappening: In the last step, רבי יוסי הגלילי used the word כריתות to teach that only a document ends a marriage. Now the גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from that same word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learned 'only a document divorces' from a different פסוק, 'וכתב לה'. So the word כריתות seems unused in their view, and the גמרא expects every word of the תורה to teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, meaning the majority of חכמים who disagree with רבי יוסי הגלילי
Severance, the word the תורה uses for a גט: 'a document of cutting off'
What do they do with it? A standard question asking how someone uses a פסוק

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this word "severance,"
phrases.notes: From the פסוק about a גט, 'סֵפֶר כְּרִיתֻת', in דברים 24:1.

phrases.english: what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the same question back on the other side: רבי יוסי הגלילי uses כריתות, so how do the רבנן use it?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from the word כריתות

steps.title: The divorce must fully cut him off from her
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use כריתות to teach that a גט must completely cut the connection between husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for the rule that a divorce must be something that cuts him off from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן learn a different rule from כריתות: a גט must truly end the bond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'cutting off' tells us that a גט cannot leave the husband with an ongoing hold on his wife. If something still ties her to him, it is not real כריתות.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it, meaning the word is used to teach a different law
Something that cuts, a full and complete separation
Between him and her

phrases.english: They need it
for something that cuts between him and her,

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְדָבָר הַכּוֹרֵת בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by giving the רבנן a different use for כריתות
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כריתות teaches that a גט must fully cut the bond between husband and wife

steps.title: A ברייתא: forever conditions versus thirty-day conditions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the rule in action. A גט with a condition that binds her forever is not כריתות, but a condition for thirty days is.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'This is your divorce on condition that you never drink wine,' or 'on condition that you never go to your father's house' — that is not severance. 'For thirty days' — that is severance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows what 'fully cutting him off' means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband makes the גט depend on her never doing something, he controls her life forever, so she is not truly cut off from him. A limited condition, like thirty days, eventually ends, so the separation is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
On condition that
Forever
Thirty days, a limited time

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן learn from כריתות that a גט must leave no lasting hold of the husband over his wife, so a condition that binds her forever ruins the גט.
steps.confusionAlert: Conditions are not the problem in themselves. The thirty-day condition is fine. Only a condition that never ends spoils the כריתות.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you will not drink wine,"
"on condition that you will not go
to your father's house ever" —
this is not severance.
"For all thirty days" —
this is severance.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטֵּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁלֹּא תִּשְׁתִּי יַיִן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up and illustrates the rule from step 19
steps.raayaObject: That כריתות means a complete cut with no lasting hold
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about conditions placed on a גט

steps.title: Where does רבי יוסי הגלילי learn the 'full cut' rule?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יוסי הגלילי already used כריתות for something else, where does he get the rule that a גט must fully cut the bond?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the opposite question. רבי יוסי הגלילי used כריתות to teach 'only a document divorces,' so where does he learn the 'full cut' rule?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees with the 'full cut' rule. The רבנן get it from כריתות, but רבי יוסי הגלילי has already used that word, so he needs another source.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili?
phrases.notes: Short for: where does he learn that a גט must fully cut the bond, since he used כריתות for something else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side gets the rule that the רבנן just learned from כריתות
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי יוסי הגלילי's source for the 'full cut' rule

steps.title: He learns it from the longer form of the word
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from the fact that the תורה wrote the longer word כריתות instead of the short כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He derives it from כרת versus כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי reads two teachings into the word. The basic meaning gives one law, and the extra, longer form gives another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have written the short form כרת. Writing the fuller form כריתות adds something, and from that addition he learns the 'full cut' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The short, basic form of 'cut'
He derives it, he learns it from

phrases.english: From 'karet' versus 'keritut'
phrases.notes: The תורה could have used the short word כרת but wrote the longer כריתות. That extra length teaches the second rule.

phrases.english: he derives it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra form כריתות, instead of כרת, teaches the 'full cut' rule

steps.title: And what do the רבנן do with the longer form?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן deal with the difference between כרת and כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן do not also learn something extra from the longer word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the extra form can teach a law, the רבנן could use it for the 'full cut' rule and keep כריתות free for 'only a document divorces.' So the גמרא asks why they don't.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Short for: what do they learn from the extra form of the word?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 22's method back on the רבנן
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the רבנן treat the difference between כרת and כריתות

steps.title: The רבנן do not read anything into the longer form
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן do not learn anything from the difference between כרת and כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not find meaning in כרת versus כריתות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן do not treat the longer form as teaching anything extra. This closes the discussion about the word כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, the word כריתות teaches only one law, the 'full cut' rule. That is why they need a different פסוק, 'וכתב לה', to teach that only a document divorces.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not mean anything to them, they do not learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on two rules: only a document divorces, and a גט must fully cut the bond. They only disagree about which words of the פסוק teach which rule.

phrases.english: 'Karet' versus 'keritut'
does not signify anything to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 and closes the discussion of the word כריתות
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן do not learn anything from the longer form of the word

steps.title: Why not learn one method from the other two together?
steps.stepSummary: Earlier it was shown that one way of making קידושין cannot be learned from just one other way. The גמרא asks why we can't learn it from the other two combined.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot be derived from one; let one be derived from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the three ways to make קידושין: כסף, שטר and ביאה. If each is written in the תורה, couldn't one of them have been learned from the other two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, each method was shown to have a weakness that blocks learning it from just one other method. But when two sources are put together, each one's weakness can be covered by the other. So the תורה might not need to write all three.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one, learning one method from a single other method
Cannot be derived
Let it be derived
From two, learning from two sources together

phrases.english: One cannot be derived from one,
phrases.notes: This refers back to the earlier part of the daf, where each way of making קידושין was shown not to come from a single other way.

phrases.english: let one be derived from two!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כריתות discussion and goes back to the earlier question of why the תורה needs all three ways of making קידושין
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תורה needed to write all three ways of making קידושין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining two sources covers each one's weakness, so one method should be learnable from the other two

steps.title: Testing the options: could document be learned from the other two?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by asking which one would be learned, and it starts testing the options. First option: the תורה would leave out שטר and learn it from כסף and ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one would be derived? Let the Merciful One not write 'document,' and derive it from these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by testing each method, one at a time, to see whether it could come from the other two. This step sets up the first test case, שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is going to be that no method can be dropped. To show this, the גמרא tries removing each one. First it imagines the תורה never wrote שטר and asks whether כסף and ביאה together could teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one would be derived?
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
A document, here one of the ways to make קידושין
These ones, here meaning כסף and ביאה

phrases.english: Which one would be derived?
Let the Merciful One not write 'document,'
and derive it from these —
phrases.notes: 'These' means the other two ways, כסף and ביאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי תֵּיתֵי? לָא לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 25 by checking each method, starting with שטר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Testing each option to show that none can be dropped
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe שטר could come from כסף and ביאה together
steps.terutzMaskana: The test continues in the next step, where the idea is rejected

steps.title: Money and intercourse give her much more benefit
steps.stepSummary: שטר cannot come from כסף and ביאה, because both of those give the woman a lot of הנאה, and a document does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about these? Their benefit is great.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the idea of learning שטר from the other two. כסף and ביאה share a feature that שטר lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both כסף and ביאה give the woman real enjoyment or benefit, so maybe that is why they work. A document is just paper and gives her almost nothing, so we could not assume it works too. This is why the תורה had to write שטר on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: What about these? The start of a rejection: these are different
Since, because they have a special feature
Their benefit is great

steps.confusionAlert: This only rules out learning שטר. The גמרא has not yet tested learning כסף or ביאה from the other two.

phrases.english: What about these?
Their benefit is great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea proposed in step 26
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the option of learning שטר from כסף and ביאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כסף and ביאה share a feature, great הנאה, that שטר lacks, so the two together cannot teach שטר

steps.title: Intercourse cannot be learned from money and a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the second option, learning ביאה from כסף and שטר, and rejects it because כסף and שטר are much broader ways of acquiring.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the תורה had not written ביאה, and we learned it from כסף and שטר. That fails, because כסף and שטר have something special: they acquire in many areas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps testing which way of making קידושין could be left out of the תורה. Now it tries leaving out ביאה and shows why that does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כסף and שטר are used to buy many things, such as fields and other property, so they are strong, wide-reaching ways of acquiring. ביאה only acquires a wife. Something with a narrow, unusual use cannot be learned from two broad tools, so this option fails.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ who wrote the תורה
These, meaning the other two ways
Their acquiring power is wide; they work in many areas

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write [acquisition] through intercourse,
and let it be derived from these,
phrases.notes: "These" are כסף and שטר, the two ways that would still be written.

phrases.english: [but] what about these?
They are special, since their acquisition is great.
phrases.notes: He means כסף and שטר can acquire many things, like land, not just a wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּבִיאָה וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second option in the test that began in Step 26. Step 27 rejected leaving out שטר; this step rejects leaving out ביאה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning ביאה from the combination of כסף and שטר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כסף and שטר share a feature ביאה lacks: they have wide acquiring power in many areas.

steps.title: Money cannot be learned from intercourse and a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the third option, learning כסף from ביאה and שטר, and rejects it because those two can work against the woman's will.
steps.simpleTranslation: Suppose the תורה had not written כסף, and we learned it from ביאה and שטר. That fails, because ביאה and שטר have something special: they can work even against her will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option, leaving out כסף, and shows why that also fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבם acquires his יבמה through ביאה even if she does not agree. A שטר, in the form of a גט, can end a marriage without her agreement. Since both have a forceful power that כסף does not seem to have, כסף cannot be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Against her will
A widow whose husband died without children, who falls to his brother
A document of divorce

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write [acquisition] through money,
and let it be derived from these,
phrases.notes: This time "these" are ביאה and שטר.

phrases.english: [but] what about these?
They are special, since they work against her will.
phrases.notes: A יבם acquires a יבמה through ביאה without her consent, and a גט can divorce her without her consent.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּכֶסֶף וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last option in the test from Step 26, following the rejection of the ביאה option in Step 28.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning כסף from the combination of ביאה and שטר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ביאה and שטר can work against the woman's will; כסף seemingly cannot.

steps.title: But money also works against a girl's will with a Hebrew maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on Step 29: כסף can also work against a girl's will, because a father can sell his daughter as an אמה העבריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that כסף also works against her will, as with a Hebrew maidservant whom her father sells without asking her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises an objection to the last rejection. It points to a case where כסף works without the girl's agreement, which would put כסף in the same group as ביאה and שטר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 said כסף is different because it never works against a woman's will. Here the גמרא brings a counterexample: a father receives money and sells his young daughter as a maidservant without her consent. If this case counts, the difference disappears, and כסף could be learned from ביאה and שטר after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say; it introduces a possible objection
A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant

phrases.english: And if you say
[that] money also [works] against her will,
in the case of a Hebrew maidservant,
phrases.notes: Her father can sell her for money without asking her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כֶּסֶף נָמֵי בְּעַל כׇּרְחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference given in Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 29 that כסף never works against a woman's will.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: with an אמה העבריה, כסף takes effect without the girl's consent, so כסף would share the feature of ביאה and שטר.

steps.title: In marriage, money never works against her will
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the maidservant case does not count, because in marriage itself we never find כסף working against a woman's will. This closes the whole test: none of the three ways can be learned from the other two.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least in marriage, we have not found that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the objection from Step 30 and keeps the difference from Step 29. This finishes the section showing that each way of making קידושין needs its own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אמה העבריה case is about selling a girl into service, not about marriage. In marriage, כסף only works with the woman's agreement, while ביאה (with a יבמה) and שטר (a גט) can work in marriage matters without it. So the difference stands, and כסף cannot be learned from the other two.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage
At least, in any case
We have not found

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three ways of making קידושין, כסף, שטר and ביאה, has a special feature the other two lack. That is why the תורה had to write all three and could not leave one out.

phrases.english: In marriage, at least, we have not found [this].
phrases.notes: He means: with marriage, כסף never takes effect without the woman's agreement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 30 and so upholds Step 29, completing the answer to Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the comparison to the relevant area (marriage only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since כסף works against a girl's will with an אמה העבריה, it shares the feature of ביאה and שטר and could be learned from them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only cases within marriage count. In marriage כסף never works against her will, so the difference stands and כסף needs its own source.

steps.title: רב הונא: the wedding canopy also makes קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that חופה can make קידושין, and proves it with a קל וחומר from כסף, using the law of eating תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: חופה makes קידושין, learned through a קל וחומר. If כסף, which does not let a woman eat תרומה, makes קידושין, then surely חופה, which does let her eat תרומה, should make קידושין!
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. רב הונא suggests a fourth way of making קידושין, the חופה, and gives a logical proof for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof compares how strong כסף and חופה are. A non-כהן's daughter who was betrothed with כסף to a כהן may not yet eat תרומה, but after חופה she may. Since חופה is stronger than כסף in this respect, רב הונא reasons it should at least be able to do what כסף does, which is make קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The wedding canopy; bringing the bride into the husband's domain
A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat
Lets her eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new question: are כסף, שטר and ביאה the only ways to make קידושין, or can חופה also work? The rest of the sugya will test רב הונא's קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The wedding canopy acquires, [learned] from an a fortiori argument:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה כֶּסֶף שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַאֲכִיל בִּתְרוּמָה – קוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: If money, which does not let [her] eat תרומה, acquires,
[then] the wedding canopy, which does let [her] eat תרומה,
is it not logical that it should acquire?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא חוּפָּה קוֹנָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous section was completed in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חופה makes קידושין, as shown by a קל וחומר from כסף: חופה lets a woman eat תרומה and כסף does not, so חופה should be able to make קידושין just as כסף does.

steps.title: By Torah law, money already lets her eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's claim that כסף does not let a woman eat תרומה. It brings עולא, who says that by Torah law a betrothed woman does eat תרומה, and that only a גזירה of the חכמים stops her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that money does not let her eat תרומה? עולא said that by Torah law, a Jewish woman betrothed to a כהן may eat תרומה. The פסוק says that a person a כהן buys with his money may eat, and she was 'bought' with his money. The only reason the חכמים said she may not eat is a גזירה. While she still lives in her father's house, someone might pour her a cup of תרומה wine, and she might share it with her brothers and sisters, who are not allowed to eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the starting point of רב הונא's קל וחומר. It shows that כסף does let a woman eat תרומה, at least by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's קל וחומר needed a difference between כסף and חופה: חופה lets her eat תרומה and כסף does not. עולא shows that by Torah law there is no difference, because a woman betrothed with כסף may eat. She is held back only by a גזירה of the חכמים, so the 'weakness' of כסף disappears and the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Lets her eat; here, makes her allowed to eat תרומה
By Torah law, as opposed to a rule of the חכמים
A betrothed woman, after קידושין but before חופה
The acquisition of his money; someone a כהן acquired with money
A protective rule made by the חכמים to keep people away from a Torah prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: עולא agrees that in practice a betrothed woman does not eat תרומה. The point is only that the Torah itself allows it, so כסף is not truly 'weaker' than חופה in this area.
steps.whyThisMatters: A קל וחומר only works if the 'weaker' side is really weaker. Once עולא shows the gap is only a rule of the חכמים, the proof as first stated cannot stand.

phrases.english: And does money not let her eat?
But didn't Ulla say:
By Torah law,
a betrothed daughter of a non-כהן
eats תרומה,
as it is said:
"And if a כהן acquires a person,
the acquisition of his money"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:11

phrases.english: and this woman is "the acquisition of his money."
And why did they say she does not eat?
It is a decree, in case they pour her a cup
in her father's house
and she gives it to her brother and her sister to drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the premise of רב הונא's קל וחומר in Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's assumption that כסף does not let a woman eat תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולא shows that by Torah law, a woman betrothed with כסף does eat תרומה, and only a גזירה of the חכמים stops her. So כסף is not weaker than חופה in this area, and the קל וחומר breaks.

steps.title: Rebuilding the argument: money does not finish the acquisition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the תרומה version and restates רב הונא's קל וחומר in a new way. The new version begins: כסף, which does not 'finish' the acquisition, still acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is how he argued: if money, which does not complete the woman's acquisition, still acquires her...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing how רב הונא's proof is worded. This line is only the first half of the new קל וחומר, and the second half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of comparing כסף and חופה on eating תרומה, the new version compares them on finishing the acquisition. כסף only makes the first stage, אירוסין, and does not bring her fully into marriage. Yet כסף still acquires. That sets up the coming conclusion that חופה, which does finish the acquisition, should surely be able to acquire.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the old version and offers a new one
He argued this way; this is how the proof should be worded
Completes; fully finishes bringing her into marriage
Acquires; here, makes קידושין

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Wait for the second half, about חופה, before deciding what the proof means.

phrases.english: Rather, he argued like this:
phrases.notes: "He" is רב הונא, from Step 32; the גמרא is fixing how his proof was worded.

phrases.english: If money, which does not complete the acquisition,
still acquires,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to Step 33 by restating רב הונא's קל וחומר on a new basis.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the proof: changing what the קל וחומר is built on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר rested on כסף not letting her eat תרומה, which עולא's teaching knocked down.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר now rests on כסף not finishing the acquisition. Even so, it still acquires, which leads to a קל וחומר for חופה.
